title: Compatibility of pointed-algebra and residue-triple strict henselizations
statement: Let $R$ be a local commutative ring, $K$ a chosen separable closure of $R/\mathfrak m_R$, with its compatible $R$-algebra structure, and $C$ an $R$-algebra satisfying the pointed-algebra colimit predicate [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. There is a point $p$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with prime ideal $\mathfrak m_R$ and an algebra structure making $K$ a separable closure of the scheme residue field $\kappa(p)$. For this structure the residue-triple ring diagram [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples] has a universal cocone with vertex $C$, and every composite $R\to B\to C$ along a cocone leg is the original structural map $R\to C$.

source.place: Tag 04GW, triples identified with pointed etale algebras; specialized to the maximal ideal of a local ring

proof.text: Take p to be the maximal ideal. Use the affine scheme residue-field identification to identify its residue field with the fraction field of R/m; since R/m is a field, this is R/m. Transport the chosen K-algebra and separable-closure structures along this identification.

Send a triple (B,q,phi) to the etale R-algebra B pointed in K by evaluation at q followed by phi. The compatibility equation says this is an R-algebra map. Conversely take the kernel q of a pointed-algebra map B to K. Its contraction is m because R to K is the quotient R to R/m followed by an injective field map. Factor B to K through B/q and extend uniquely to its fraction field by sending b/s to its image divided by the nonzero image of s. This gives the required residue embedding. Both categories have exactly the maps commuting with R and K, so these assignments are fully faithful and essentially surjective and identify the ring diagrams.

The triples category is filtered, hence nonempty and connected. Transport the universal algebra cocone in the hypothesis along the preceding equivalence and its vertex isomorphism to C. To see that it is a ring colimit, take any ring cocone: connectedness makes the composites R to B to its vertex equal. Their common value gives an R-algebra structure on that vertex, with every leg an algebra map. The algebra colimit universal property now supplies a unique ring map; any ring map satisfying the leg equations automatically commutes with R. This proves the ring universal property and the required structural-map compatibility.
